section_title: Why can Christ’s priesthood provide lasting assurance?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 20 And none of this happened without an oath. For others became priests without an oath, 21 but Jesus became a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him: “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever.’” 22 Because of this oath, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.

23 Now there have been many other priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office. 24 But because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood. 25 Therefore He is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.

context_lines: God’s oath confirms Christ’s priesthood, so Jesus is the guarantee of a better covenant. The promise rests on the God who will not change His mind.

The earlier priests served in succession because death ended their service. Jesus continues forever. The word [translated permanent](https://biblehub.com/greek/531.htm) describes a priesthood that does not pass to a successor.

The result concerns the people who approach God through Him: He can save completely because He always lives to intercede. His continuing life is not a distant fact about heaven; it is the ground of His continuing care for them.
common_interpretation_lines: [Calvin](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/calvin/hebrews/7.htm) and [Wesley](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-epistle-to-the-hebrews/) both understand Christ’s enduring life as the ground of His continuing priesthood and intercession. The [Catholic Catechism, paragraph 662](https://www.vatican.va/content/catechism/en/part_one/section_two/chapter_two/article_6/he_ascended_into_heaven_and_is_seated_at_the_right_hand_of_the_father.html), likewise teaches that He permanently exercises His priesthood in God’s presence on behalf of those approaching through Him.

Calvin emphasizes the lasting security of His saving work; Wesley describes salvation reaching the guilt, power and consequences of sin. Their shared point is the sufficiency of the living Christ for those who come to God through Him.
god_plan_lines: [Romans 8:31–39](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/8.htm) also joins Christ’s death, resurrection and intercession with assurance for His people. Their hope rests in the living Savior and God’s love, rather than a priest whose service will eventually end in death.

[Hebrews 10:19–22](https://biblehub.com/bsb/hebrews/10.htm) develops the result: His people can draw near to God through the way Jesus has opened. The enduring priesthood serves God’s purpose of bringing people into His presence.
current_position_lines: Our study [Who Shepherds the Church?](https://thewayofscripture.com/studies/who-shepherds-the-church.html) understands Christ’s priesthood as permanent, with no successor needed because He lives forever. Believers approach God through Him. The study therefore rejects a clergy class acting as a necessary spiritual mediator between believers and God, while retaining elders who teach, correct and care for the church.
